text.p: Randy Johnson pitched no-hit ball for seven-plus innings and matched a season high with 15 strikeouts Sunday, carrying the Seattle Mariners to a 2-0 shutout of the Detroit Tigers.

Johnson (9-1) extended his personal winning streak to five games and did not allow a hit until Phil Nevin hit the first pitch he saw in the eighth into left field for a clean single. Johnson, who has struck out 15 or more batters 11 times in his career, walked three batters.
"It was a bad pitch and he hit it," Johnson said about Nevin's single. "I don't know if it was my best game, but I've got to feel good about it."
Bobby Ayala allowed one hit in the ninth but still recorded his third save. Seattle has won six of its last seven games since a three-game losing streak.
Brian Moehler (4-5) was the tough-luck loser for Detroit, giving up one run and six hits over eight innings. He has lost four of his last five decisions at home.

Johnson, who threw a two-hitter against Toronto last Monday, extended his scoreless inning streak to 29 and lowered his ERA to 2.45. He also struck out 10 or more batters for the third time in his last four starts and for the 74th time in his career.
Seattle got a run in the sixth, when Ken Griffey scored on an RBI grounout by Paul Sorrento. The Mariners added a run in the ninth on an RBI single by Russ Davis.

In Boston, Wil Cordero, Reggie Jefferson and Nomar Garciaparra each drove in two runs in a nine-run fourth inning explosion that let the Boston Red Sox erase a five-run deficit and roll to a 12-6 victory over the Cleveland Indians.
Every Boston starter had at least one hit and Garciaparra went 3-for-5 to lead the 16-hit attack.
Joe Hudson (1-0), who had his contract purchased by the Red Sox from Triple-A Pawtucket before the game, pitched three scoreless innings to earn the win.
Cleveland's Chad Ogea (5-5) failed to hold the 5-0 lead. He lasted 3 1/3 innings and surrendered six runs and six hits.

In Kansas City, Tom Goodwin's two-run single keyed a four-run second inning and Tim Belcher allowed two runs over six solid innings, helping the Kansas City Royals pull out a 4-2 triumph over the Texas Rangers.
Texas starter Ken Hill (4-4) gave up the four-run second to take the loss.

Belcher (7-6) gave up six hits with two walks and six strikeouts to win his second straight after three consecutive losses. Mike Williams retired the final two batters to post his first major-league save.

In Minneapolis, Tim Salmon homered and drove in four runs and Garret Anderson delivered a two-out, two-run single in a five-run seventh inning as the Anaheim Angels rallied from a four-run deficit and defeated the Minnesota Twins, 8-6.
A bases-clearing double by Paul Molitor off starter Dennis Springer (4-2) in the fourth inning had given the Twins a 6-2 lead.
Troy Percival worked a hitless ninth with two strikeouts for his fifth save.

In New York, David Cone allowed one run over seven innings and Paul O'Neill and Tino Martinez homered, leading the New York Yankees to a 3-1 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers, and a sweep of their three-game series.
Cone (7-3) gave up six hits, walked two and struck out nine, improving to 13-1 at Yankee Stadium as a Yankee. Mariano Rivera pitched a scoreless ninth for his major-league leading 19th save.
Jeff D'Amico (2-3) allowed two runs and six hits in six innings as the Brewers lost for the 10th time in their last 11 games in New York.
In Chicago, Roberto Alomar homered and Tony Tarasco rapped a run-scoring single in the sixth inning, helping the Baltimore Orioles hold off the Chicago White Sox for a 2-1 victory.
Jimmy Key (10-1) allowed a run, six hits and a walk and struck out a season-best nine.
Armando Benitez pitched a perfect eighth and Randy Myers got the final three outs for his 19th save, matching Mariano Rivera for the league lead.
Danny Darwin (2-3) gave up two runs and eight hits with three walks and two strikeouts but took the loss.

In Toronto, Geronimo Berroa hit a three-run homer and Mark McGwire added a two-run shot, his 24th of the season, as the Oakland Athletics held on to defeat the Toronto Blue Jays, 7-5, and salvage a split of their four-game series.
Don Wengert (3-3), making his first start on the road this season, pitched five hitless and scoreless innings, striking out five and walking two for the victory.
Luis Andujar (0-2) surrendered seven runs -- six earned -- and nine hits over four innings as he suffered his second loss in as many starts.
